transcript:
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Rylan Barton.
Five British nationals described as terror suspects have now been released on bail.
They were detained yesterday near a British military base used by the U.S. to launch strikes
on Iran.
That location prompted concerns about a connection to the Middle East, as NPR's Lauren Freire
reports.
British counterterrorism officials say the men are still under investigation for explosives
and terrorism offenses, and that authorities are investigating multiple lines of inquiry,
including whether the suspects were working for Iran, Russia, or other non-state groups
"knowingly or unknowingly."
Iran's embassy in London denies any involvement, saying malicious speculation only fuels Iranophobia.
The men, Londoners, all in their mid-20s, were detained in the middle of the night near
RAF Royal Air Force Base, Fairford, west of London.
It's been the target of anti-war protesters as well.
Lauren Freire, NPR News, London.
The Education Department has dropped a Biden-era rewrite of Title IX — that's the law that
prohibits discrimination in schools based on sex — and NPR's Corey Turner reports.
The move is mostly a formality, making clear that the interpretation of Title IX now being
enforced is the one drafted in 2020 during the first Trump administration.
There are lots of differences between the Obama and Biden-era interpretations of Title
IX, and now the law under Trump, but some of the clearest concern how colleges handle
allegations of sexual harassment and assault on campus.
The Trump guidelines require that accusers meet a higher standard of proof, demanding
clear and convincing evidence compared to the Obama-era preponderance of the evidence.
The Trump rules also require that in sexual assault cases, schools hold live hearings,
where both the accused and the accuser can be cross-examined.
Corey Turner, NPR News.
CDC employees say the agency's work is being hampered by job cuts.
The staff union says the CDC lost a third of its workers since last spring, when the
Trump administration began slashing the federal workforce.
From WABE in Atlanta, Jess Mador has more.
The CDC lost 30 percent, or more than 3,800 employees, between March of 2025 and May of
this year, according to the report. That includes hundreds of employees who were terminated,
put on administrative leave, or who opted for retirement.
The Trump administration has maintained the cuts eliminated waste, fraud, and abuse in
the government.
In an emailed statement, a spokesperson for the American Federation of Government Employees
Union says the job cuts continue and amount to a dismantling of the public health infrastructure
designed to respond quickly to threats.
For NPR News, I'm Jess Mador in Atlanta.
Pope Leo XIV says concerns about AI going rogue should be taken seriously.
The comments come after President Trump called the concerns a hoax.
Leo says that safety issues raised by AI experts should be discussed and acted on.
This is NPR.
The Trump administration is asking the Supreme Court to allow restrictions on gender-affirming
care in prisons.
For now, the emergency appeal comes after lower courts blocked the policy, which stems
from an executive order from President Trump.
The administration argues the policy was properly adopted and the judge overstepped.
It halts surgeries, hormones, and social accommodations while allowing mental health therapy.
A towering figure of Caribbean music who performed as Mighty Sparrow died in New York at age 91,
and PR's Felix Contreras reports Slinger Francisco became the face and voice of Trinidadian Calypso.
Slinger Francisco earned his stage name Mighty Sparrow for his energetic dance moves during
his earliest performances in the dual island nation of Trinidad and Tobago, and it was
during the island's legendary Calypso Carnival competitions when his legend began to take
shape by way of lyrics that were socially conscious about everyday life on the island.
Mighty Sparrow was considered the Calypso king of the world by his fans, and recognized
by the island's cultural institutions for spreading the sound of the West African-based
Calypso from the Caribbean to the world.
Felix Contreras, NPR News.
Weathered wooden beams, possibly from a 19th century shipwreck, have emerged from the sand
along Nantucket's southern shore after a powerful nor'easter battered the island.
The remains surfaced near an area where pieces believed to belong to the Warren Sawyer had
previously emerged.
This is NPR News from Washington.

topics.text: Five British nationals described as terror suspects released on bail near RAF Fairford military base
Education Department drops Biden-era Title IX rewrite, reinstates Trump administration's 2020 interpretation
CDC lost over 3,800 employees since March 2025 due to Trump administration workforce cuts
Pope Leo XIV says concerns about AI going rogue should be taken seriously
Trump administration asks Supreme Court to allow restrictions on gender-affirming care in prisons
Mighty Sparrow, legendary Trinidadian calypso musician, dies in New York at age 91
Weathered wooden beams possibly from 19th century shipwreck emerge along Nantucket's southern shore
